definition.name: The Reluctant One — from hollow conformity to self-authored savior.
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Identity — Who am I, really? — and the tension between a scripted destiny and a chosen self.
definition.summary: Neo begins as a man split between two names, submitting flatly to an office ultimatum (ev-005) and refusing the 'One' label even as a voice imposes it (ev-008). Each pressure — Smith's interrogation (ev-007), the unbearable truth of the farmed world (ev-013), the failed jumps (ev-016), and the Oracle's private verdict (ev-023) — strips his old certainty without yet giving him a new one. The chain resolves only when, after dying for Morpheus, he rejects the death fate Smith pronounces (ev-039), seizes the identity on his own terms (ev-045), and rises into flight as a self-authored man (ev-047). Because he denies being the One even while committing to the rescue (ev-032), the plot argues that identity is chosen, not conferred.

chain.why_in_plot: It is the plot's baseline: Neo answers a job ultimatum with 'flat, deferential compliance,' enacting the 'hollow conformity' the throughline must move him out of.
chain.caused_by_previous: Sets the chain moving. The office ultimatum is the status-quo identity that later pressures will strip away.

chain.why_in_plot: Guided to a ledge he 'cannot bring himself to cross,' Neo is shown as still bound by his old limits—conformity's inability to act—before any new self exists.
chain.caused_by_previous: The deferential office worker of ev-005 is the one the raid now corners; his compliance turns to paralysis at the ledge.

chain.why_in_plot: Smith's interrogation lays out Neo's 'two lives' and literally seals his mouth—the external pressure beginning to strip his old certainty.
chain.caused_by_previous: The man cornered at the ledge in ev-006 is seized and brought into the interrogation room where his split identity is named.

chain.why_in_plot: A voice imposes 'the One' label and demands 'Yes,' and Neo refuses it—the plot's core tension (scripted destiny vs. chosen self) first stated outright.
chain.caused_by_previous: The implanted, mouthless captive of ev-007 is reclaimed; the identity being denied here is the one Smith's interrogation in ev-007 framed.

chain.why_in_plot: The 'unbearable truth of the farmed world' dissolves Neo's assumptions about himself and his era, stripping old certainty without yet supplying a new one.
chain.caused_by_previous: The red-pill choice (ev-010) and rebirth (ev-011) lead to this revelation; it is the 'farmed world' pressure the summary names as a stripping agent.

chain.why_in_plot: The failed jump is a named stripping pressure: his mind will not yet author the impossible, so his old self-image keeps failing.
chain.caused_by_previous: The dismantled assumptions of ev-013 are tested physically; the rooftop jump exposes that belief has not yet replaced certainty.

chain.why_in_plot: The 'Oracle's private verdict' is the named pressure that withholds a new identity; Neo carries a death-prophecy he is ordered to keep, deepening the not-yet-resolved state.
chain.caused_by_previous: The failed jumps (ev-016) leave him unmade; the private verdict he receives here deepens the identity vacuum the chain tracks.

chain.why_in_plot: The plot's thesis in action: Neo commits to the rescue while denying he is the One, making identity a chosen wager on a man rather than a conferred prophecy.
chain.caused_by_previous: Stripped of certainty by ev-023's verdict, Neo's only remaining ground is a choice—the rescue he cannot justify logically.

chain.why_in_plot: At the edge of death Neo 'refuses the name and fate Smith pronounces' and summons his own surge—the death-fate rejection the summary names as the turning point.
chain.caused_by_previous: The chosen commitment of ev-032 (a wager on a man) now manifests as self-authored power that rejects the fate imposed on him.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo 'seizes the identity on his own terms,' destroying Smith from within—identity taken, not received.
chain.caused_by_previous: The surge of self-authored power in ev-039 culminates here: having refused Smith's verdict, he now overwrites the Agent entirely.

chain.why_in_plot: He 'rises into flight as a self-authored man,' completing the arc from hollow conformity to chosen savior.
chain.caused_by_previous: The seized identity of ev-045 is now lived openly—flight is the outward proof of the self-authored identity he took in ev-045.

definition.name: The Rescue of Morpheus — a wager on a man against all logic.
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: Morpheus's self-sacrifice to buy Neo's escape (ev-025) is answered when Morpheus is captured (ev-026) and the surviving crew prepares to pull his plug rather than die for a lost cause. Neo interrupts that self-preserving logic and commits to going back in, explicitly denying he is the One so the mission rests on faith in a man rather than prophecy (ev-032). That decision conditions everything after — Trinity converting grief into command, the helicopter assault, Morpheus shot mid-dive and caught by the wrist (ev-034), and the rooftop belief confirmed (ev-035) — proving the sacrifice horn of the dilemma by action.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's origin point: Morpheus's self-sacrifice 'to buy Neo's escape' (the summary's ev-025) is the debt the rest of the plot answers. Material: 'Morpheus bursts through, pins the Agent down, and orders Trinity to get Neo out—choosing to give his own life so the others can escape.'
chain.caused_by_previous: Chain-initiating event: the firefight in the wall and the Agent ambush on Neo force Morpheus's choice to trade his life, setting the rescue dilemma in motion.

chain.why_in_plot: The sacrifice produces its consequence: Morpheus is captured, creating the 'lost cause' the crew then prepares to abandon. Material: 'Morpheus starts dominant strangling Agent Smith, then loses ground—head-butting Smith but tak[ing]...' (his capture).
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus's decision to hold the wall so the others escape (ev-025) leaves him behind and overrun, directly enabling his capture here.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's decisive turn—the summary's anchor. Neo interrupts the crew's self-preserving logic (pulling Morpheus's plug) and commits to going back in, explicitly denying he is the One so the mission 'rests on faith in a man rather than prophecy.' Material: 'Neo stops the plug from being_pull
chain.caused_by_previous: The capture (ev-026) plus the crew's readiness to cut Morpheus loose set up the self-preservation-vs-sacrifice collision that Neo breaks; his denial of being the One reframes the rescue as a wager on the man Morpheus just proved worth dying for (ev-025).

chain.why_in_plot: The commitment is executed: the helicopter assault and the mid-dive catch are the action that 'proves the sacrifice horn of the dilemma.' Material: 'Neo drops the helicopter onto the executive office and guns down Agents... finds Morpheus unresponsive and has to extract him by force... Smith shoots
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's wager (ev-032) conditions everything after—Trinity 'converting grief into command' and the assault launch flow from that decision; the physical rescue is the enacted form of his choice to go back in.

chain.why_in_plot: The aftermath confirms the plot's thesis: 'rooftop belief confirmed.' Morpheus reinterprets prophecy around the man they just saved. Material: 'Morpheus cuts him off and reinterprets both the prophecy and Trinity's silence as confirmation.'
chain.caused_by_previous: The successful extraction and the wrist-catch (ev-034) leave the crew alive on the roof, where the confirmed survival becomes the grounds for Morpheus's belief—belief that only exists because the rescue happened.

definition.name: Cypher's betrayal — resentment traded for comfortable illusion.
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Truth vs. a comfortable lie, and meaning vs. pleasure — is an unbearable reality worth a purposeful struggle, or is ignorant comfort the wiser trade?
definition.summary: Cypher reframes Morpheus's prophecy as 'a body count' (ev-020) and, savoring a fabricated steak, bargains with Smith to be re-plugged into the lie, modeling the self-preservation and comfortable-lie horns of the story's dilemmas. His treachery escalates causally from a dropped trace phone (ev-021, ev-023) to open murder aboard the ship — killing Apoc and Switch and delivering Morpheus to the Agents (ev-029) — nearly erasing the crew entirely. His arc is the counter-argument to Neo's: where Neo moves from hollow routine toward a cause worth dying for, Cypher trades meaningful freedom for soft, meaningless comfort and is destroyed by Tank, who survived (ev-029, ev-030).

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's seed: Cypher, dressing resentment over the dinner as a joke, fails to rattle Trinity and reaches for the Oracle to force Morpheus's faith into something verifiable — the comfortable-lie horn of the dilemma taking root as envy of Neo.
chain.caused_by_previous: This is the first entry; it sets the chain moving by establishing Cypher's resentment and his turn toward a verifiable, comfortable certainty against Morpheus's faith.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher reframes Morpheus's prophecy as 'a body count' and, savoring a fabricated steak, bargains with Agent Smith to be re-plugged into the lie — the exact act the plot names as modeling self-preservation and the comfortable lie.
chain.caused_by_previous: His private resentment (ev-017) escalates into active treason: having already sought a verifiable escape from faith, he now consummates the trade by negotiating re-insertion into the Matrix.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher covertly connects a phone and drops it in a garbage can in the alley — the dropped trace phone the plot cites as the first causal step from bargain to murder.
chain.caused_by_previous: Having struck his bargain with Smith (ev-020), Cypher begins servicing it by planting the traceable phone that will let the Agents close in on the crew.

chain.why_in_plot: The trap closes because the Matrix is rewritten around the crew, sealing them in the Hotel Lafayette and forcing Morpheus to seize a traceable phone — the direct consequence of Cypher's planted line, driving toward the crew's near-erasure.
chain.caused_by_previous: The dropped trace phone (ev-021) enables the Agents to rewrite the Matrix around the crew and spring the trap that pins them inside the hotel.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher is present as the crew converges on the wall and Morpheus chooses to sacrifice himself so the others escape — the capture of Morpheus that Cypher's deal was designed to deliver.
chain.caused_by_previous: The trap that sealed the crew in the hotel (ev-023) forces the firefight in the wall where Morpheus gives himself up, setting up Cypher's delivery of his captive.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher is among those descending into the basement as Morpheus is overpowered and captured — the plot's 'delivering Morpheus to the Agents' moving into its execution phase.
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus's self-sacrifice in the wall (ev-025) lets the survivors flee into the basement, where Morpheus is finally taken, advancing Cypher's betrayal toward completion.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher, having separated from the street group, is already at the exit and demands to be routed to a specific phone — the traitor positioning himself ahead of the crew to strike aboard the ship.
chain.caused_by_previous: With Morpheus captured in the basement (ev-026), the survivors split to regroup, and Cypher uses the confusion to reach the exit first, priming the shipboard murders.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher climbs through the exit window and his body jerks awake aboard the ship, where he draws a concealed rifle — the transition from dropped-trace treachery to open, armed murder aboard the Nebuchadnezzar.
chain.caused_by_previous: Having reached the exit ahead of the crew (ev-027), Cypher jacks out first so he can ambush the returning members the moment they re-enter their bodies.

chain.why_in_plot: The plot's core escalation: Cypher turns quiet treachery into open murder — shooting Tank, killing Apoc and Switch, delivering Morpheus to the Agents, and standing over comatose Neo — nearly erasing the crew.
chain.caused_by_previous: Drawing the concealed rifle after waking (ev-028), Cypher immediately turns it on the crew, executing the murders his deal and positioning were built to enable.

chain.why_in_plot: The betrayal's resolution: the survivors wake to find Dozer dead and Tank wounded, and Trinity infers Tank's grief — the aftermath of Cypher's shipboard slaughter and the setup for his destruction by the Tank who survived.
chain.caused_by_previous: Cypher's murders and his stand over Neo (ev-029) leave the waking survivors to register the body count, closing the causal run from dropped phone to near-total erasure of the crew.

definition.name: The Agents' hunt — order reasserting itself against an anomaly.
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Freedom vs. determinism — can choice break a pre-scripted system, or does the system always re-capture the exception?
definition.summary: The Agents open by correcting the illusion of a successful raid and splitting to hunt Trinity (ev-001, ev-002), then systematically close every exit — corralling Neo off the ledge (ev-006), interrogating and sealing him (ev-007), and rewriting the Matrix around the crew to spring the trap (ev-023). Smith in particular treats Neo as a solvable equation, offering to erase the 'Anderson' record (ev-007) and later framing Neo's death as settled inevitability at the subway (ev-039). The hunt's causal escalation — capture of Morpheus (ev-031), the Sentinel strike ordered to seal the escape (ev-036), Smith's point-blank execution of Neo (ev-043) — exists to be broken by the one act the system cannot compute: Neo's refusal of the pronouncing fate and his destruction of Smith from within (ev-039, ev-045).

chain.why_in_plot: Opens the hunt: Agent Smith corrects the Lieutenant's belief that the raid is succeeding, telling him his units are already dead — the Agents reasserting order against an anomaly, which is this plot's core premise.
chain.caused_by_previous: First link in the chain — no prior event; the Agents' opening correction of the illusion sets the hunt in motion.

chain.why_in_plot: The Agents split to hunt Trinity — the systematic pursuit of the anomaly begins, directly matching the plot's 'correcting the illusion' → 'splitting to hunt' opening.
chain.caused_by_previous: Follows ev-001's revelation that the raid is not succeeding; because the arrest failed and the anomaly is loose, the two agents divide their approach to close in.

chain.why_in_plot: The Agents seize Neo at the office, driving him to a window ledge he cannot cross — the plot's explicit 'corralling Neo off the ledge' beat, the system closing an exit.
chain.caused_by_previous: The hunt established in ev-002 escalates from Trinity to Neo; the systematic closing of exits now targets the next anomaly, forcing him to the ledge.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo is interrogated and sealed; Smith offers to erase the 'Anderson' record — the plot's named 'interrogating and sealing him' beat, with Smith treating Neo as a solvable equation.
chain.caused_by_previous: Directly follows ev-006's capture: having corralled Neo off the ledge, the Agents now hold him and attempt to negotiate/rewrite his record.

chain.why_in_plot: The Trap Springs — the plot's named 'rewriting the Matrix around the crew to spring the trap' beat; the system re-captures the exception by reshaping reality.
chain.caused_by_previous: The hunt's pressure (from ev-007 onward) escalates from one target to the whole crew; the system rewrites the environment to seal them, continuing the closing of exits.

chain.why_in_plot: The Agents take Morpheus into custody and drive him toward breaking — the plot's named 'capture of Morpheus,' a key escalation of the hunt's causal chain.
chain.caused_by_previous: Follows the trap in ev-023: with the crew sealed and Morpheus sacrificing himself (ev-025) / captured (ev-026), the Agents now hold him and interrogate him.

chain.why_in_plot: Jones orders a Sentinel strike to seal the escape while Smith senses the quarry is not gone — the plot's named 'Sentinel strike ordered to seal the escape,' the system's final sealing move.
chain.caused_by_previous: Follows ev-031's capture and the subsequent rescue (ev-034): once the crew flees with Morpheus, the Agents fix the trace and order the strike to re-capture them.

chain.why_in_plot: At the subway, Smith frames Neo's death as settled inevitability and Neo refuses the pronouncing fate — the plot's named pivot, 'the one act the system cannot compute.'
chain.caused_by_previous: The Sentinel strike in ev-036 forces the crew's exit and leaves Neo trapped in the subway with Smith, producing the confrontation where Smith pronounces his fate.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo races to the phone and is stopped cold by Agent Smith's point-blank shot — part of the hunt's causal escalation the plot names, the system's final physical sealing of an exit.
chain.caused_by_previous: After breaking free at the subway (ev-039), Neo flees the tightening city; Smith closes to point-blank range and executes the settled inevitability he pronounced.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo enters Agent Smith and bursts out, destroying him — the plot's named 'destruction of Smith from within,' the exception that breaks the hunt's chain.
chain.caused_by_previous: Follows ev-043's point-blank execution and ev-044's revival: having refused the pronouncing fate, Neo returns and destroys the Agent the system sent to settle him.
